newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's SFE wheat futures ease further on rain.
newsitem.headline: Australia's SFE wheat futures ease further on rain.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange wheat futures eased further on Wednesday as continued planting rain in Australia's eastern wheat belt helped ease supply fears.
"The market was easing back a little bit on fairly widespread rain," Brendan Hillary of ANZ Futures Ltd said.
May 1997 futures edged up A$1 to A$194 a tonne on a volume of nine lots but near July lost A$2.50 to A$193 on a volume of two lots and January 1998 fell A$3.50 to A$178 on four lots.
Hillary said an eight U.S. cents a bushel decline in Chicago overnight also contributed and added that he saw Chicago's price influence growing in the near term as drought fears eased.
